question: How the original draws on battle plans: bp_settings, the tools, the mouse, what a drawing holds and how it is rendered.

addresses.name: CBattlePlanManager::OnToolPressed
addresses.comment: Observer of the seven buttons of `tools` (the button's tag, set by index 0..6 from the strip's order select, arrows, borders, icons, colors, text, erase). Tag 6, **erase**: nothing unless a plan is chosen, editable (+0x1F0) and the player's own (+0x218 = player id); deletes every selected arrow, border and icon/text of it and does not change the tool. Any other tag: for text (5) only, with a plan as above, prepares the edit box: first selected arrow -> its label's text and placing off; else first selected text -> its text and placing off; else 'New Text' into the box and settings +0xE8, placing on. EditBox_RefreshText and the box's +0x40 = 1. Then settings +0 = tag and CBattlePlanManager::UpdateToolStrip.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and read in place, field offsets cross-checked against BattlePlan_Serialize's keys and the shipped .pln files; a wrong entry would show as a mismatch of ret size or a field not matching a .pln key.

addresses.name: CBattlePlanManager::OnToolOptionPressed
addresses.comment: An entry of options_window: nothing without an editable plan of the player's; settings[1 + tool] = the entry's tag (its option index); UpdateToolStrip. **Tool colors (4)**: the chosen colour's index (+8 of the option) goes straight on every selected arrow and border (+0x154) and selected icon (+0x140), and the plan's dirty byte set. A selected text is left alone: a text has no colour of its own. (The decompiler drops those loops as unreachable; read off the disassembly at 0x40FFB7-0x410094.)

addresses.name: GraphicsView::PickGroundPoint
addresses.signature: void __thiscall GraphicsView::PickGroundPoint(void* this, float* out, void* input)
addresses.comment: A view (the idler's +0x1788, with its camera at +0x1C): unprojects the mouse (input slot 19) at the near and far planes through the view's camera matrices (slots 91 and 93) and the graphics' viewport (+0x6BC88), intersects with the plane y = 0 and writes (x, z) to out. **The result is relative to the map camera**, so a world map point is the pick plus MapCamera x_settled/y_settled; map pixels, one pixel a unit, no snapping to provinces.

addresses.name: BattlePlanToolSettings_LoadFile
addresses.comment: Parses bp_settings.txt: at the top level the four keys tool_color, tool_arrow, tool_borders, tool_icons; any other key is read and dropped. In a tool block the first key must be `icon` (its value kept as the sprite name; another key there is consumed and lost, and the icon stays empty), then `option = {...}` entries, each a new 0x34-byte (colour) or 0x44-byte option with its position in the list at +8; other keys in the block are read and dropped. An option block is read through CPersistent::Load, so a key not in LoadKey is reported unknown, not fatal. File missing: returns false, no options at all. **Nothing validates that a `type` names an object type**: drawing with one that does not exist calls through a null type (a crash, not read further).

addresses.name: BattlePlan_HitTest
addresses.signature: void __stdcall BattlePlan_HitTest(void* plan, float* point, float tolerance, float* camera)
addresses.comment: **What a click selects, one object**, tolerance 1.25. Icons and texts first, in list order: a sign with text is hit within 1.25 * length(text) * text size * 0.25 of its point, an icon within 1.25 * type scale * 0.5, and the first hit is selected and ends the test. Then arrows, then borders, each pass looking only at their control points and needing squared distance under 31.25 (25 * tolerance), the nearest point wins and an arrow's label is selected with it. Coordinates relative to the camera: object position + object's world - camera - point.
